✶The Ledger✶

Years since the first one
144
The first Labor Day parade was in New York City in 1882, a Tuesday, and about ten thousand people took an unpaid day off to march in it. The holiday has been a Monday since 1894.

✶The National Wire✶

1

Cargo Jet Overruns Runway in Miami, Five Dead

An Amazon-branded Boeing 767 from San Juan ran off the end of the runway Sunday afternoon and struck vehicles on the ground. Five others were hurt; the NTSB is on scene.

2

Armed Man Lunges at Ohio Candidate at County Fair

Amy Acton, the Democrat running for governor, was unhurt; several bystanders were knocked down and one was injured. A 38-year-old carrying two handguns was arrested.

3

Hurricane Lowell Bears Down on Kauai

The Category 3 storm passes west of the islands tonight. Hawaii is under a statewide emergency, with up to 14 inches of rain and 74-mph gusts forecast for Kauai and Niihau.

4

U.S. Envoys Make First Wartime Visit to Kyiv

Witkoff and Kushner met Zelensky by train a day after three hours with Putin, and are pushing for three-way talks. No breakthrough, but both sides called it substantive.

🏈The Gridiron🏈

Six Days to Kickoff
Bills · at Houston, Sunday 1:00 on FOX. Chauncey Gardner-Johnson is back at practice and expected to start at safety; the Texans will be without their starting right tackle. Seventh-round rookie Tommy Doman won the punting job, and Greg Dortch is the likely punt returner. First game of the Joe Brady era.
Jets · at Tennessee, Sunday 1:00 on CBS, against Robert Saleh, fired by the Jets two years ago. Geno Smith makes his first Week 1 start for New York since 2014 — the longest gap between opening starts for one team in the Super Bowl era. Rookie Cade Klubnik is the backup; first-round tight end Kenyon Sadiq is still out after an abdominal injury.

⚑The Chase⚑

Bell Ends a 33-Race Drought at Darlington
Christopher Bell passed Kyle Larson with twelve to go after Larson stayed out on old tires through a late rain stop, and won the Southern 500 by a second over teammate Ty Gibbs. Seven runner-up finishes this year, then this. Denny Hamlin, the top seed, hit the wall after contact with Michael McDowell, went a lap down, and clawed back to 18th — still the points leader, barely. Nine races left, no eliminations, most points at Homestead wins.

★The Marquee★

1

Spider-Man, Six Weekends Running

Brand New Day took about $22 million over the holiday to reach $922 million, roughly $14 million short of The Force Awakens and the all-time domestic record. It should get there by next weekend.

2

The Movie a Studio Threw Away Is a Hit

Coyote vs. Acme, finished and then shelved by Warner Bros. as a tax write-off, was rescued by a small distributor and held third place with $37 million so far.

3

Second-Best Summer Ever at the Movies

The domestic box office closes the season near $4.7 billion, a whisker short of the 2013 record, on the back of Spider-Man and The Odyssey.

☾On This Day☾

September 7, 1813 — a Troy, New York newspaper printed the earliest known use of “Uncle Sam” for the United States, borrowed from Sam Wilson, a local meatpacker stamping barrels “U.S.” for the Army during the War of 1812. He is buried in Troy.
